messages:
katy: Heads-up: I sketched a short PRD for private deploy networking responsibilities and an ops rollback plan. Need quick prioritization from platform + infra. TL;DR: define clear customer vs redwood responsibilities, minimal acceptance tests, and a fail-open rollback path.

raj: thanks katy, can you paste the acceptance criteria you currently have? we should align on measurable checks.

katy: copied below — open to edits. short checklist: 1) control plane connectivity verified from customer VPC -> redwood control-plane over TLS (mutual) 2) data plane egress path validated for model traffic (sample load) 3) DNS resolution consistent between customer and private deploy (split-horizon tests) 4) key rotation tested end-to-end. also: documentation for customer-owned NAT/BGP steps.

lee: +1 on measurable checks. suggest we add: latency SLA smoke: p95 < 150ms for local region under non-burst workload, and a throttling detection alert if token throughput drops >20% vs baseline.

sophie: we should also clarify rollback: if customer-managed networking breaks, we need a deterministic fallback. proposal: automated route to hosted inference (if allowed by customer) OR pause traffic and return 503 with structured error linking to ops playbook. which do we prefer?

raj: fallback to hosted is nicer for UX but requires contractual permission + data handling review. fallback -> pause + 503 is safer default. can we support both with an on-by-default safety toggle?

katy: new idea: have a 3-stage rollback: 1) quick soft-fail to cached KV-prefix responses (30s) 2) circuit-break to 503 with link to status + plan 3) optional redirect to hosted if customer opt-in. We'll need acceptance tests for each stage.

tim: ops-bot: runbook link? ops-bot: <link to runbook placeholder> :robot_face:

ops-bot: Automated checklists available: 
- control-plane-tls-check 
- egress-path-smoke 
- dns-split-horizon-test 
Use `./scripts/net-acceptance.sh --env private --customer <id>` to run locally.

katy: example smoke command (for doc):
```bash
# from customer network namespace
curl -v --resolve "redwood-control:443:203.0.113.2" https://redwood-control/healthz --cert client.crt --key client.key
```
Expect HTTP 200 and JSON {"status":"ok","version":"vX"}.

lee: edge case: customer with strict egress via proxy that rewrites headers and strips mTLS—how do we detect pre-launch? acceptance test should run a header-preservation check and fail if proxy strips `x-client-id`.

sophie: also need SLOs for DNS TTL behavior and cache warming. If customer TTL is high, our KV-cache warm path needs to tolerate stale DNS until cutover window. Add acceptance criteria: TTL-aware cutover plan and a max-stale tolerance of 60s.

raj: priority ask: which of these are MUST for GA vs SHOULD? my proposal: MUST = control plane TLS, egress smoke, DNS basic resolution, rollback to 503 + docs. SHOULD = hosted fallback, header-preservation tests, key-rotation automation.

katy: agreed. i'll mark PRD sections like that. action items: @lee to add latency smoke to acceptance tests, @raj to draft contract clause for hosted-fallback opt-in, @sophie to write DNS TTL cutover section, @tim to add runbook pointers and confirm script path. will send PRD in #eng-platform for quick review by EOD.

lee: FYI add one more edge case: overlapping customer subnets causing asymmetric routing. we should add a sanity route check and a diagram in the PRD.

tim: ack, will add runbook snippets + playbook steps for rollback.

katy: thanks team. small follow-ups in PRD: traffic metrics to capture for postmortem (bytes, p95 latency, 5xx ratio, token throughput). cc @ops-bot for automated collection.

ops-bot: Noted — metrics collection config template available at /infra/metrics/private-deploy-template.yaml

raj: good session. i'm locking MUSTs for GA and will tag legal for the hosted-fallback contract language.

katy: closing loop — i'll post the PRD link in this thread when ready. :sparkles:
